doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Closing remarks and the tenor sax story
summary: Closing remarks, return to Lester Young, a tenor joke and thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well this has been marvelous talking to you. I don’t know if there’s something that you’d like to talk about that I haven’t asked.
Well you asked quite a bit of stuff. I can’t think of anything off hand.
I’m glad you didn’t become a baseball catcher.
Yeah, me too. After I heard Lester, that did it.
That’s really interesting too that you happened to hit upon that first recording.
I know it. And I had no idea who it was because Jones-Smith, that doesn’t tell you anything. But I found out.
Wow. Well I’m glad you played the trombone instead of the tenor sax, because you’ve played with so many great people. Best of luck and keep doing it.

Well you know I bought a tenor just to see what “Blue and Sentimental” would feel like playing. And this guy that has a music store in New Haven, Sol Libro, he called me for a gig and he says, “you’ll never find it, you better meet me at the store.” So I said okay I’ll show up early. So I brought the tenor and I brought it in the store. And he says, “what’s that?” I said, “my tenor.” He says, “I thought you played trombone?” So I said “really?”
So he’d had a heart attack recently so I said wait a minute, I just wanted you to evaluate the horn.
Don’t give him another one. Good story. Well listen thanks so much for your time today.
It’s been a great pleasure meeting you.
Thanks for bringing your material here.
